title: Generation of single-cell and single-nuclei suspensions from mouse brains
author: Lee, Zhang, et al.
materials:
Timing: 30–60 min
1.All dissection tools and Dounce homogenizers should be autoclaved or sterilized using acceptable practices, and proper PPE should be worn throughout the protocol.2.Prepare isoflurane chamber setup and/or load 0.05 mL Euthasol per mouse into syringe(s) for anesthesia.3.If generating single-cell suspensions, use a Bunsen burner to fire polish the tips of Pasteur pipettes, creating some with large bore openings (∼600 μm, opening should be clearly visible) and some with small bore openings (∼300 μm, opening should be barely visible). Test the flow speed by pipetting water up and down through fire polished Pasteur pipette.4.Prepare the following solutions fresh on the day of experiment (depending on the desired procedure) and keep all solutions on ice throughout the procedure:a.Embryonic brain dissections: Prepare the artificial cerebral spinal fluid (ACSF) solution and carbogenate (bubble) with 5%:95% CO2:O2. If generating single-cell suspensions, be prepared to make the Pronase Solution and Cell Reconstitution Solution after brain dissection.b.Adult brain dissections: Prepare NMDG High-Mg2+ Solution and NMDG Activity-blocking Solution, place on ice and keep carbogenated with 5%:95% CO2:O2. If sectioning brains, immerse brain matrix in ice or prepare vibratome for sectioning. If generating single-cell suspensions, prepare solutions from the Papain Dissociation Kit per manufacturer’s instructions.c.Single-nuclei suspensions.i.For downstream applications analyzing mRNA only (e.g., RNA-seq): Prepare RNA-only Nuclei Wash Buffer, RNA-only Nuclei Lysis Buffer and RNA-only Nuclei Resuspension Buffer.ii.For downstream applications analyzing DNA only (e.g., ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag, ChIP-seq, etc.): Prepare DNA-only Nuclei Wash Buffer, DNA-only Nuclei Lysis Buffer. If performing 10x Genomics ATAC-seq, also prepare the DNA-only Diluted Nuclei Buffer.iii.For downstream applications analyzing DNA and mRNA (e.g., Multiome): Prepare the Multiome Nuclei Wash Buffer and Multiome Nuclei Lysis Buffer. If performing 10x Genomics Multiome, also prepare the Multiome Diluted Nuclei Buffer.
Note: While we have not published on the Multiome technique, we have generated high quality data with the 10x Genomics Multiome kit using the solutions and protocol described below.

Note: For all solutions below, always keep on ice. Final volumes should be adjusted depending on number of samples.

steps.title: Sterilize tools and wear PPE
steps.instruction: Autoclave or otherwise sterilize all dissection tools and Dounce homogenizers; don appropriate personal protective equipment for the entire procedure.

steps.title: Set up anesthesia
steps.instruction: Prepare an isoflurane chamber and load 0.05 mL Euthasol per mouse into a syringe for intraperitoneal injection (≈270 mg/kg, 50 µL per 30 g mouse).

steps.title: Fire‑polish Pasteur pipettes
steps.instruction: Using a Bunsen burner, fire‑polish Pasteur pipette tips to create large‑bore openings (~600 µm, clearly visible) and small‑bore openings (~300 µm, barely visible). Test flow by pipetting water up and down through each tip.

steps.title: Prepare tissue‑specific solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare all solutions fresh on the day of the experiment, keep them on ice, and carbogenate (5% CO₂ : 95% O₂) where indicated.

substeps.instruction: Embryonic brain: make artificial cerebral spinal fluid (ACSF) and carbogenate; if generating single‑cell suspensions, prepare Pronase Solution and Cell Reconstitution Solution after dissection.

Adult brain: make NMDG High‑Mg²⁺ Solution and NMDG Activity‑blocking Solution, keep on ice and carbogenate; if sectioning, chill brain matrix or set up vibratome; if generating single‑cell suspensions, prepare Papain Dissociation Kit reagents per manufacturer.
Single‑nuclei suspensions: prepare the appropriate wash, lysis and resuspension buffers for RNA‑only, DNA‑only, or Multiome applications (see detailed buffer steps).

steps.title: Make RNA‑only Nuclei Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 547.68 mg sucrose (320 mM), 11.92 mg HEPES (pH 8.0, 10 mM), 12.5 µL CaCl₂ (25 mM), 3.22 mg magnesium‑acetate (3 mM), 1 µL EDTA (0.1 mM), 5 µL DTT (1 mM) and RNase‑free water to a final volume of 5 mL. Keep on ice. (DTT is Eye Damage 1, Skin Irritation 1.)

steps.title: Make RNA‑only Nuclei Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 990 µL of the RNA‑only Nuclei Wash Buffer with 10 µL IGEPAL CA‑630 (0.1% final). Bring to 1 mL total volume per sample. Keep on ice. (IGEPAL CA‑630 is Acute Toxicity 4, Eye Damage 1, etc.)

steps.title: Make RNA‑only Nuclei Resuspension Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL BSA (1% final from 10 % stock), 5 µL RNase Inhibitor (0.2 U/µL final, 40 U/µL stock), and 895 µL PBS; bring to 1 mL total per sample. Keep on ice.

steps.title: Make DNA‑only Nuclei Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 50 µL 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 7.4, 10 mM), 10 µL 5 M NaCl (10 mM), 15 µL 1 M MgCl₂ (3 mM), 50 µL 10 % Tween‑20 (0.1 % final), 750 µL 10 % BSA (1.5 % final) and RNase‑free water to 5 mL total. Keep on ice.

steps.title: Make DNA‑only Nuclei Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 990 µL DNA‑only Nuclei Wash Buffer with 10 µL IGEPAL CA‑630 (0.1% final) to a final volume of 1 mL per sample. Keep on ice. (IGEPAL hazard as above.)

steps.title: Make DNA‑only Diluted Nuclei Buffer
steps.instruction: For 10x ATAC‑seq only: combine 50 µL Nuclei Buffer (20×, from kit) with 950 µL nuclease‑free water; total 1 mL per sample. Keep on ice.

steps.title: Make Multiome Nuclei Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Use the DNA‑only Nuclei Wash Buffer (4.87 mL) and add 5 µL DTT (1 M, 1 mM final) and 125 µL RNase Inhibitor (40 U/µL, 1 U/µL final) to reach 5 mL total. Keep on ice. (DTT hazard as above.)

steps.title: Make Multiome Nuclei Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 990 µL Multiome Nuclei Wash Buffer with 10 µL IGEPAL CA‑630 (0.1% final) to 1 mL total per sample. Keep on ice. (IGEPAL hazard as above.)

steps.title: Make Multiome Diluted Nuclei Buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 50 µL Nuclei Buffer (20×, from kit), 1 µL DTT (1 M, 1 mM final), 25 µL RNase Inhibitor (40 U/µL, 1 U/µL final) and 924 µL nuclease‑free water; total 1 mL per sample. Keep on ice. (DTT hazard as above.)

steps.title: Harvest adult mouse brain
steps.instruction: Deeply anesthetize P21‑or‑older mice with Euthasol (270 mg/kg, 50 µL per 30 g mouse, IP). Confirm lack of toe‑pinch response, decapitate, peel skin, remove skull, expose brain, and place the brain in a petri dish containing carbogenated NMDG High‑Mg²⁺ Solution on ice.

steps.title: Slice brain with matrix
steps.instruction: Place the brain in a pre‑chilled stainless‑steel 0.5 mm mouse brain matrix on ice; firmly depress the razor blades through all slots to generate coronal slices; carefully remove the blades, collect desired slices, and transfer them to a petri dish with carbogenated NMDG Activity‑blocking Solution on ice.

steps.title: Slice brain with vibratome
steps.instruction: If needed, trim excess anterior/posterior tissue; glue the brain to the vibratome plate and let the glue dry 30–60 s; submerge the plate in a vibratome chamber filled with ice‑cold NMDG High‑Mg²⁺ Solution that is continuously carbogenated; cut 300–400 µm sections and transfer desired sections to a petri dish with carbogenated NMDG Activity‑blocking Solution on ice.

steps.title: Dissect regions from slices
steps.instruction: Using forceps, micro‑dissect the desired regions (e.g., striatum, cortex, hippocampus) from each slice and transfer them to properly labeled 5 mL round‑bottom tubes or petri dishes. Optional: perform dissection under a fluorescent dissecting scope for reporter lines. Optional: for nuclei‑only workflows, place tissue directly into a 1.5 mL tube, flash‑freeze on dry ice, and store at –80 °C (do not freeze for cell suspensions).

steps.title: Whole‑mount brain dissection
steps.instruction: After anesthesia and decapitation (as in step 14), place the brain ventral side down in a Sylgard‑coated petri dish containing NMDG High‑Mg²⁺ Solution; pin through the cerebellum and anterior forebrain; use curved forceps to peel the cortex anterolaterally and lay it flat to expose hippocampus and ventral structures.

steps.title: Collect regions for nuclei or cells
steps.instruction: Remove cortex, hippocampus, striatum, or other ventral structures as needed and place them into petri dishes with NMDG Activity‑blocking Solution on ice. Optional: use fluorescence to guide collection; optional: flash‑freeze tissue for nuclei‑only storage as described above.

steps.title: Prepare suspension for 10x RNA‑seq
steps.instruction: Aim for ~15,000 cells or nuclei per 10× reaction.

substeps.instruction: With FACS: collect ~15,000 cells/nuclei into a 1.5 mL LoBind tube containing 10 µL RNA‑only Nuclei Resuspension Buffer; use 43.2 µL of this suspension for the 10x RNA‑seq reaction (final volume ≈45 µL).
Without FACS: count cells/nuclei on a hemocytometer or automated counter, dilute to 1,000 cells/nuclei µL⁻¹, and use 15 µL of this suspension for the 10x RNA‑seq reaction.

steps.title: Prepare nuclei for ATAC‑seq / Multiome
steps.instruction: For ATAC‑seq or Multiome, process nuclei as follows.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge nuclei at 500 g for 10 min at 4 °C in a swinging‑bucket rotor.
Carefully remove supernatant, leaving <20 µL in the tube, and resuspend the nuclei in this residual volume.
Count nuclei on a hemocytometer (e.g., 2 µL sample + 8 µL PBS + 10 µL Trypan Blue).
Dilute the nuclei to 3,000 nuclei µL⁻¹ using DNA‑only Diluted Nuclei Buffer (for ATAC‑seq) or Multiome Diluted Nuclei Buffer (for Multiome).
Use 5 µL of the diluted nuclei suspension for the corresponding 10x Genomics ATAC‑seq or Multiome reaction.
